claim: During human forebrain development, neural progenitor cells (NPCs) in the ventricular zone (VZ) undergo asymmetric cell divisions to produce a self-renewed progenitor cell and differentiating daughter cells.
source: During human forebrain development, neural progenitor cells (NPCs) in the ventricular zone (VZ) undergo asymmetric cell divisions to produce a self-renewed progenitor cell, maintaining the potential to go through additional rounds of cell divisions, and differentiating daughter cells, populating the developing cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of human forebrain development, drawing on established knowledge of developmental neuroscience.

claim: In the embryonic rodent brain, preferential inheritance of the pre-existing (older) centrosome to the self-renewed progenitor cell is required to maintain stem cell properties and ensure proper neurogenesis.
source: Previous work in the embryonic rodent brain suggested that the preferential inheritance of the pre-existing (older) centrosome to the self-renewed progenitor cell is required to maintain stem cell properties, ensuring proper neurogenesis.
evidence: This claim references previous work in rodent models, indicating it is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The older mother centrosome is preferentially inherited towards self-renewed NPCs in human embryonic stem cell-derived regionalised forebrain organoids.
source: Using a novel, recombination-induced tag exchange-based genetic tool to birthdate and track the segregation of centrosomes over multiple cell divisions in human embryonic stem cell-derived regionalised forebrain organoids, we show the preferential inheritance of the older mother centrosome towards self-renewed NPCs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data using the Centriolin-RITE system in organoids.

claim: Aberration of asymmetric segregation of centrosomes by genetic manipulation of Ninein alters fate decisions of NPCs in human cortical organoids.
source: Aberration of asymmetric segregation of centrosomes by genetic manipulation of the centrosomal, microtubule-associated protein Ninein alters fate decisions of NPCs and their maintenance in the VZ of human cortical organoids.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data from Ninein knockdown experiments.

claim: Around gestational week 5 in the developing human brain, NPCs transition from symmetric to asymmetric divisions.
source: Around gestational week (GW) 5 in the developing human brain (corresponding approximately to embryonic day (E) 11.5 in the mouse embryo), NPCs, at this developmental stage referred to as radial glia or apical progenitor cells, transition from an expansive phase into a neurogenic phase and shift their mode of division from symmetric to asymmetric divisions (Götz and Barde, 2005; Malatesta et al., 2008; De Juan Romero and Borrell, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature on human brain development.

claim: Centrosomes duplicate once per cell cycle in a semi-conservative way, producing one centrosome that is older and functionally more mature than the other one.
source: The centrosome duplicates once per cell cycle that occurs in a semi-conservative way, producing one centrosome that is older and functionally more mature than the other one.
evidence: This is established knowledge about centrosome biology.

claim: In the mouse developing cortex, self-renewing NPCs inherit the older, more mature centrosome while the newborn neuron inherits the new, daughter centrosome.
source: Indeed, in the mouse developing cortex self-renewing NPCs appear to inherit the older, more mature centrosome while the newborn neuron inherits the new, daughter centrosome (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Randomisation of centrosome inheritance leads to premature depletion of NPCs from the VZ in mouse cortical development.
source: Notably, randomisation of centrosome inheritance leads to premature depletion of NPCs from the VZ, indicating functional relevance of asymmetric centrosome inheritance during mouse cortical development (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Mind-bomb1 is preferentially enriched at the younger centrosome and asymmetrically segregates with it into the differentiating daughter cell.
source: How asymmetric centrosome inheritance affects cellular fate is only poorly understood but, for example, recent work showed that Mind-bomb1, a Notch signalling regulator, is preferentially enriched at the younger centrosome, asymmetrically segregates with it into the differentiating daughter cell, and thereby potentially promotes stemness via Notch signalling activation in surrounding NPCs (Tozer et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tozer et al., 2017.

claim: The human brain relies on species-specific molecular regulators and genetic pathways.
source: However, it is clear that the human brain relies on species-specific molecular regulators and genetic pathways (Bystron et al., 2008; Pinson and Huttner, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bystron et al., 2008 and Pinson and Huttner, 2021.

claim: Centriolin localises to the subdistal appendages of the mother centriole.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas9 (Ran et al., 2013) we inserted the RITE construct into hESCs immediately upstream of the terminal stop codon of Centriolin, a protein that localises to the subdistal appendages of the mother centriole (Gromley et al., 2003; Gromley et al., 2005; Kashihara et al., 2019; Chong et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing Centriolin localization.

claim: The Centriolin yeast ortholog, Nud1, has limited turnover on the pre-existing yeast spindle pole body.
source: The Centriolin yeast ortholog, Nud1, has previously been shown to have limited turnover on the pre-existing yeast spindle pole body (Lengefeld et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lengefeld et al., 2017.

claim: Centriolin-tdTomato was properly localising to the centrosome as shown by staining with Pericentrin.
source: Indeed, tdTomato-positive dots were observed in each cell and NeonGreen was detectable within 24 hr after recombination induced by electroporation of Cre recombinase expressing plasmid; staining with the centrosomal marker protein Pericentrin showed that Centriolin-tdTomato was properly localising to the centrosome (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B with Pericentrin co-staining.

claim: Centriolin-tdTomato co-localised to one of the two centrioles.
source: In line with the known behaviour of Centriolin as a subdistal appendage of the mother centriole, Centriolin-tdTomato co-localised to one of the two centrioles.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data with GFP-Centrin-1 and is consistent with known Centriolin behavior.

claim: Centriolin-tdTomato signal was present in prophase cells but diminished by metaphase.
source: Examination of cells at different stages of mitosis showed that Centriolin-tdTomato signal was present in prophase cells but diminished by metaphase (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Centriolin-tdTomato protein remained localised to the centrosome throughout mitosis despite fluorescence quenching.
source: To investigate whether this was due to loss of Centriolin-tdTomato protein or quenching of fluorescence, we stained for tdTomato, which revealed that Centriolin-tdTomato protein remained localised to the centrosome throughout mitosis (Figure 1D), indicating that RITE-tagged Centriolin allows for tracking centrosomes in human cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: CEP164 co-localised with Centriolin-tdTomato in day 35 forebrain organoids.
source: Day 35 organoids were fixed and stained with the centrosomal marker CEP164 to check for correct co-localisation of RITE-tagged Centriolin within organoids. Indeed, CEP164 co-staining confirmed co-localisation with Centriolin-tdTomato (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Ventricle-like structures in organoids are easily identifiable by the clustering of Centriolin-tdTomato-labelled centrosomes belonging to SOX2-positive NPCs in the VZ.
source: Ventricle-like structures at the centre of cortical units were easily identifiable by the clustering of Centriolin-tdTomato-labelled centrosomes, belonging to SOX2-positive, NPCs in the VZ (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Recombined centrosomes exhibited variable quantities of the older, Centriolin-tdTomato protein.
source: Presence of Centriolin-NeonGreen was detected both inside and outside the ventricle, indicating successful recombination (Figure 2B). Interestingly, we observed centrosomes with varying NeonGreen-to-tdTomato ratios, indicating centrosomes of varied ages.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mixed tdTomato and NeonGreen centrosomes were observed at longer time points (>20 days) after recombination, indicating that centriolin was remarkably stable on the centrosome.
source: Such mixed tdTomato and NeonGreen centrosomes were observed at longer time points (>20 days) after recombination indicating that centriolin was remarkably stable on the centrosome, labelled with CEP164.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data over time.

claim: There is a higher proportion of orange centrosomes (older) in the ventricle compared to outside the ventricle.
source: Comparison between these two regions revealed a higher proportion of orange centrosomes in the ventricle compared to outside the ventricle (Figure 2G, H, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by manual analysis of centrosome colors shown in Figure 2G and 2H.

claim: There is a higher proportion of green centrosomes (younger) outside the ventricle compared to inside the ventricle.
source: The inverse was observed for green centrosomes, whereas there was no difference seen in the localisation of yellow centrosomes, similar to what was observed in the absolute number of each centrosome colour (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by manual analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: VZ centrosomes had a lower proportion of NeonGreen signal compared to their non-ventricular progeny.
source: This analysis showed that VZ centrosomes had a lower proportion of NeonGreen signal compared to their non-ventricular progeny (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, Figure 2—source data 2), corroborating the previous results obtained by manual grading.
evidence: This is supported by unbiased fluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Green centrosomes co-localised with TBR1+ cells (neuronal progeny).
source: TBR1 was excluded from the NPC dense VZ and indeed, green centrosomes co-localised with TBR1+ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Knockdown of Ninein can randomise centrosome inheritance by preventing centriole maturation without impeding the cells' ability to divide.
source: Previous work identified that a knockdown of Ninein can randomise inheritance by preventing centriole maturation, without impeding the cells' ability to divide (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Ninein-targeting shRNA significantly decreased Ninein signal compared to scrambled shRNA in HEK cells.
source: Analysis of the intensity of the Ninein signal showed a significant decrease between scrambled and Ninein-targeting shRNAs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental validation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: There was a decrease in the proportion of SOX2-positive cells upon Ninein knockdown in organoids.
source: Strikingly, within the H2B-CFP+ population (cells expressing either Ninein or scrambled shRNA) we found a decrease in the proportion of SOX2-positive cells upon Ninein knockdown, which corresponded with a significant increase in the neuronal, CTIP2-positive population.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from organoid electroporations.

claim: There was a significant increase in the neuronal, CTIP2-positive population upon Ninein knockdown in organoids.
source: Strikingly, within the H2B-CFP+ population (cells expressing either Ninein or scrambled shRNA) we found a decrease in the proportion of SOX2-positive cells upon Ninein knockdown, which corresponded with a significant increase in the neuronal, CTIP2-positive population.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: Knockdown of Ninein leads to precocious neuronal differentiation of NPCs in the VZ.
source: These data suggest that knockdown of Ninein, and therefore possibly randomisation of centrosome inheritance, leads to precocious neuronal differentiation of NPCs in the VZ (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data supported by the observed increase in CTIP2+ cells and decrease in SOX2+ cells.

claim: Ninein knockdown caused an increase in old (orange) non-ventricular centrosomes compared to scrambled control.
source: Remarkably, we observed a shift in the localisation of the old centrosomes in the Ninein knockdown condition as compared to the scrambled, with an increase in old (orange) and a decrease in young (green) non-ventricular centrosomes in the Ninein knockdown cells as compared to the scrambled condition (Figure 4C, D, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by centrosome color analysis shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: Ninein knockdown caused a substantial increase in green (young) centrosomes in ventricular regions.
source: This corresponded with the reverse seen in younger (green) centrosomes, where Ninein knockdown caused a substantial increase in green centrosomes in ventricular regions (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by centrosome color analysis shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: Ninein plays a role in the inheritance of the older centrosome in cells of the VZ.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Ninein plays a role in the inheritance of the older centrosome in the cells of the VZ and that aberration of Ninein, here through shRNA-mediated knockdown, leads to segregation of the older centrosome also into non-ventricular areas, associated with impaired NPC behaviour (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Ninein knockdown effects.

claim: Asymmetric inheritance of centrosomes is an evolutionary conserved mechanism during cortical formation.
source: The data we present here show that asymmetric inheritance of centrosomes is an evolutionary conserved mechanism during cortical formation that may be of critical relevance for human brain development by maintaining the proper cellular behaviour of human NPCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings in human organoids combined with knowledge of similar mechanisms in other species.

claim: Non-random inheritance of centrosomes based on their age has been reported in the developing cortex of flies, chickens, and mice.
source: Previous work showed that there is non-random inheritance of centrosomes based on their age in the developing cortex of flies (Januschke et al., 2011; Ranjan et al., 2019; Sunchu and Cabernard, 2020), chickens (Tozer et al., 2017), and mice (Wang et al., 2009; Paridaen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work in different species.

claim: Centrosomes are the primary microtubule organising centres of metazoan cells.
source: Centrosomes are the primary microtubule organising centres of metazoan cells and provide the contractile forces required for mitosis in most human cells (Bornens, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about centrosome function, supported by citation.

claim: At mitosis, the older and younger centrosome will always be asymmetrically segregated to one of the two daughter cells.
source: At mitosis, the older and younger centrosome will always be asymmetrically segregated to one of the two daughter cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about centrosome segregation during cell division.

claim: Drosophila neuroblasts inherit the younger centrosome and pass on the older centrosome to their differentiating daughter cells.
source: In contrast, Drosophila neuroblasts inherit the younger centrosome and pass on the older centrosome to their differentiating daughter cells (Januschke et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Januschke et al., 2011.

claim: The mother centrosome is quicker to reassemble the primary cilium because it is already decorated with the distal appendages from the previous interphase.
source: Indeed, it has been shown that the mother centrosome is quicker to reassemble the primary cilium, likely because it was already decorated with the distal appendages from the previous interphase (Paridaen et al., 2013), which has been shown to be critical for NPC cellular behaviour.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Paridaen et al., 2013.

claim: Overexpression of the centrosomal protein AKNA increased centrosomal microtubule organisational activity, destabilised the apical junction, and caused NPCs to delaminate from the apical surface.
source: Indeed, previous work showed that overexpression of the centrosomal protein AKNA increased centrosomal microtubule organisational activity, destabilised the apical junction, and caused NPCs to delaminate from the apical surface and migrate out of the VZ.
evidence: This claim references previous work, indicating citation support.

claim: The mother centrosome anchors to the apical membrane via the distal appendage protein CEP83.
source: Furthermore, the mother centrosome was shown to anchor to the apical membrane via the distal appendage protein CEP83 (Shao et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shao et al., 2020.

claim: Loss of CEP83 causes impaired apical anchorage of the centrosome, disorganisation of microtubules, increase in NPC proliferation and subsequent enlargement of the cortex.
source: Loss of CEP83 causes impaired apical anchorage of the centrosome, disorganisation of microtubules, increase in NPC proliferation and subsequent enlargement of the cortex.
evidence: This claim references findings about CEP83 function, likely from the same citation context.

claim: A substantial number of human variants and mutations associated with microcephaly have been identified in genes associated with centrosome function and structure.
source: For example, disturbance of asymmetric inheritance of centrosomes could play a causative role in microcephaly where indeed a substantial number of human variants and mutations have been identified in genes associated with centrosome function and structure (Faheem et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Faheem et al., 2015.

claim: A recent cell type-specific analysis of centrosomal proteomes identified a large number of proteins, previously implicated with neurodevelopmental disease, to be associated with centrosomes.
source: Strikingly, a recent cell type-specific analysis of centrosomal proteomes identified a large number of proteins, previously implicated with neurodevelopmental disease, to be associated with centrosomes (O'Neill et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to O'Neill et al., 2022.

claim: Brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells recapitulate early steps of human brain development.
source: Recent methodological advances such as the generation of brain organoids, derived from human pluripotent stem cells, recapitulate early steps of human brain development, allowing for novel approaches to characterise the principles of cortical development in human tissues (Lancaster et al., 2013; Di Lullo and Kriegstein, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lancaster et al., 2013 and Di Lullo and Kriegstein, 2017.

claim: Cortical organoids render a perfect system to study asymmetric cell divisions as the stem cells and their progeny segregate spatially.
source: Cortical organoids render a perfect system to study asymmetric cell divisions as the stem cells and their progeny segregate spatially with the NPCs lining the ventricle and the neurons surrounding the NPCs (Qian et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Qian et al., 2016 and describes a methodological advantage.

claim: The Centriolin-RITE tool allows for birthdate and track the segregation of centrosomes over multiple cell divisions in human cells.
source: Using a novel, recombination-induced tag exchange-based genetic tool to birthdate and track the segregation of centrosomes over multiple cell divisions in human embryonic stem cell-derived regionalised forebrain organoids, we show the preferential inheritance of the older mother centrosome towards self-renewed NPCs.
evidence: This is a methodological claim supported by the experimental design and data presented.

claim: The RITE system uses tdTomato and NeonGreen fluorescent proteins that originate from two evolutionary distinct species.
source: Additionally, we designed the RITE system to use fluorescent proteins tdTomato and NeonGreen that originate from two evolutionary distinct species: Discosoma sp. and Branchiostoma lanceolatum, respectively (Shaner et al., 2004; Shaner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citations to the fluorescent protein sources.

claim: Photoconversion requires the tagged proteins to be targeted with a laser, which requires surgery or tissue extraction.
source: Photoconversion requires the tagged proteins to be targeted with a laser, which requires surgery or tissue extraction to allow for laser accessibility.
evidence: This is a methodological limitation of photoconversion approaches based on technical knowledge.

claim: Photoconversion inevitably produces phototoxic events in cells which may alter their behaviour.
source: Furthermore, photoconversion inevitably produces phototoxic events in cells which may alter their behaviour.
evidence: This is a known limitation of photoconversion techniques based on established knowledge.

claim: The Centriolin-RITE birthdating tool can be activated in a spatial and temporal dependent manner by the use of tamoxifen-inducible Cre approaches.
source: The Centriolin-RITE birthdating tool can be activated in a spatial and temporal dependent manner by the use of tamoxifen-inducible Cre approaches.
evidence: This is a methodological feature of the tool described in the study.

claim: Inheritance of the old centrosome may reduce aberrant mitotic events as the mother centrosome had participated previously in at least one successful mitosis.
source: One potential reason could be that inheritance of the old centrosome may reduce aberrant mitotic events as the mother centrosome had participated previously in at least one successful mitosis, suggesting that the centrosome is capable of producing a daughter centriole, nucleating microtubules, and facilitating normal chromosome segregation, while the newly synthesised daughter centrosome is newer and less 'tested' as it has never produced a functional centrosome.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed to explain the observed phenomenon.

claim: The older centrosome is inherited by self-renewing NPCs in mouse and human cortical development, and by the daughter cell in budding yeast.
source: In support of this notion, the older centrosome is inherited by self-renewing NPCs in mouse (Wang et al., 2009) and, as we here show, in human cortical development, and by the daughter cell in budding yeast (Pereira et al., 2001; Lengefeld et al., 2017), which is considered the stem cell.
evidence: This claim combines findings from the current study with citations to previous work in mouse and yeast.

claim: Drosophila neuroblasts produce less progeny and therefore have lower selective pressure to maintain their fitness.
source: One may speculate that Drosophila neuroblasts produce less progeny and therefore have lower selective pressure to maintain their fitness.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed to explain the different pattern in Drosophila.

claim: The maintenance of NPCs in the VZ requires a delicate balance of centrosomal function at the apical surface.
source: These data indicate that the maintenance of NPCs in the VZ requires a delicate balance of centrosomal function at the apical surface.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited work on AKNA and CEP83.

claim: Inheritance of the older centrosome could be one mechanism by which NPCs regulate the balance of centrosomal function.
source: Inheritance of the older centrosome could be one mechanism by which NPCs regulate this balance.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed based on the study's findings.

claim: Removing Ninein from the centrosome could alter the balance of centrosomal function and lead to the older centrosome being inherited to a non-ventricle destined cell.
source: Removing Ninein from the centrosome could alter this balance and lead to the older centrosome being inherited to a non-ventricle destined cell.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the Ninein knockdown experimental results.

claim: Centrosomes act as one of the key signalling centres of the cell.
source: Additionally, it is becoming apparent that centrosomes act as one of the key signalling centres of the cell (Arquint et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Arquint et al., 2014.

claim: Consistent retention of particular centrosome allows asymmetric signalling pathways to be established and could facilitate the coordination of other cellular asymmetries.
source: Consistent retention of particular centrosome allows of such asymmetric signalling pathways to be established and could facilitate the coordination of other cellular asymmetries (Royall and Jessberger, 2021).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis supported by citation to Royall and Jessberger, 2021.

claim: Disturbance of asymmetric inheritance of centrosomes could play a causative role in microcephaly.
source: For example, disturbance of asymmetric inheritance of centrosomes could play a causative role in microcephaly where indeed a substantial number of human variants and mutations have been identified in genes associated with centrosome function and structure (Faheem et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis connecting the study's findings to human disease, supported by citation.

claim: Disrupting retention of the pattern of centrosome inheritance affects proper neurogenesis in human forebrain organoids.
source: We here identify that human NPCs show asymmetric inheritance of centrosomes and that disrupting retention of the pattern of centrosome inheritance affects proper neurogenesis in human forebrain organoids.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's primary findings supported by experimental data.

claim: Asymmetric cell divisions result in two daughter cells with different fates and cellular behaviour during neurogenesis.
source: Asymmetric divisions result in two daughter cells with different fates and cellular behaviour: one daughter remains in the VZ and retains the ability to self-renew, comparable to the mother cell. The other daughter cell migrates along the basal process of their sister cell, out of the VZ and either directly begins the process of neuronal differentiation or initiates additional rounds of symmetric, differentiating cell divisions producing two neurons (at this stage referred to as intermediate progenitors or basal progenitor cells) (Noctor et al., 2004; Hansen et al., 2010; Gao et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Noctor et al., 2004; Hansen et al., 2010; Gao et al., 2014.

claim: The centrosome might play a central role in distinct fates of daughter cells upon neurogenic, asymmetric cell divisions.
source: Exactly how differential fates of sister cells are established remains not completely elucidated; however, previous work showed that the centrosome might play a central role in distinct fates of daughter cells upon neurogenic, asymmetric cell divisions (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Centrosomes are unbound organelles comprised of two centrioles connected by a flexible linker and surrounded by pericentriolar material.
source: Centrosomes are unbound organelles comprised of two centrioles connected by a flexible linker and surrounded by a dynamic protein matrix called pericentriolar material.
evidence: This is established knowledge about centrosome structure.

claim: Centriolin-RITE allows for discrimination of pre-existing vs. newly synthesised Centriolin based on red vs. green fluorescence.
source: As the reading frame is maintained, Centriolin will be constitutively tagged with tdTomato. LoxP recombination with Cre recombinase will excise the first section containing tdTomato, causing Centriolin to be tagged with NeonGreen, and allowing for the discrimination of pre-existing vs. newly synthesised Centriolin based on red vs. green fluorescence.
evidence: This is a description of how the Centriolin-RITE system works, supported by the experimental design.

claim: NeonGreen was detectable within 24 hr after recombination induced by electroporation of Cre recombinase expressing plasmid.
source: Indeed, tdTomato-positive dots were observed in each cell and NeonGreen was detectable within 24 hr after recombination induced by electroporation of Cre recombinase expressing plasmid; staining with the centrosomal marker protein Pericentrin showed that Centriolin-tdTomato was properly localising to the centrosome (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Correct localisation of RITE-tagged Centriolin was confirmed by live imaging of hESCs following electroporation of GFP-Centrin-1.
source: Correct localisation of RITE-tagged Centriolin was confirmed by live imaging of hESCs following electroporation of GFP-Centrin-1, which localised to the centrioles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental validation supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The RITE construct consists of tdTomato flanked by LoxP sites and followed by NeonGreen.
source: With the aim to birthdate and track the segregation of centrosomes over multiple cell divisions in human cells we created a novel genetic tool based on the recombination-induced tag exchange (RITE) system (Hotz et al., 2012), consisting of the red fluorescent protein tdTomato flanked by LoxP sites and followed by a second section containing the green fluorescent protein NeonGreen (with each section ending with a terminal stop codon followed by a 3′UTR or a T2A Neo, respectively) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the genetic construct design, supported by Figure 1A.

claim: The RITE system is based on the recombination-induced tag exchange system described by Hotz et al., 2012.
source: With the aim to birthdate and track the segregation of centrosomes over multiple cell divisions in human cells we created a novel genetic tool based on the recombination-induced tag exchange (RITE) system (Hotz et al., 2012), consisting of the red fluorescent protein tdTomato flanked by LoxP sites and followed by a second section containing the green fluorescent protein NeonGreen (with each section ending with a terminal stop codon followed by a 3′UTR or a T2A Neo, respectively) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hotz et al., 2012.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 was used to insert the RITE construct into hESCs immediately upstream of the terminal stop codon of Centriolin.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas9 (Ran et al., 2013) we inserted the RITE construct into hESCs immediately upstream of the terminal stop codon of Centriolin, a protein that localises to the subdistal appendages of the mother centriole (Gromley et al., 2003; Gromley et al., 2005; Kashihara et al., 2019; Chong et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by citation to Ran et al., 2013.

claim: A stable expression cassette of ERT2-CRE-ERT2 was introduced from the human safe harbour locus AAVS1.
source: To simplify and facilitate Cre recombinase-mediated recombination without the need of transfection or electroporation we used CRISPR/Cas9 to introduce a stable expression cassette of ERT2-CRE-ERT2 from the human safe harbour locus Adeno-associated virus site 1 (AAVS1; Roemer et al., 2016), which we used for subsequent experiments.
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by citation to Roemer et al., 2016.

claim: Centrosomes outside of the VZ were more sparsely distributed than those in the VZ.
source: Centrosomes outside of the VZ were more sparsely distributed.
evidence: This is an observation from imaging data of organoids.

claim: Ventricle-like structures in organoids are tubular or spherical in nature.
source: As ventricle-like structures in organoids are tubular or spherical in nature, this dimension collapse produces a circle of centrosomes, where multiple Z planes show a ring (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an observation about organoid structure supported by imaging data.

claim: HEK cells transfected with shRNA and GFP-Ninein revealed a significant reduction in GFP-Ninein in cells expressing Ninein-targeting shRNA compared to scrambled shRNA.
source: Furthermore, HEK cells transfected with shRNA and GFP-Ninein (Chen et al., 2003) revealed a significant reduction in GFP-Ninein in cells expressing Ninein-targeting shRNA compared to scrambled shRNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F, Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This is an experimental validation supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Constructs expressed human Ninein-targeting shRNA or a scrambled shRNA under the U6 promoter, as well as an H2B-CFP.
source: We produced constructs that expressed human Ninein-targeting shRNA or a scrambled shRNA under the U6 promoter, as well as an H2B-CFP to facilitate identification of targeted cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a methodological description of the constructs used.

claim: Day 35 organoids were electroporated with Ninein-targeting and control shRNA-expressing constructs into the VZ.
source: Ninein-targeting and control shRNA-expressing constructs were then electroporated into the VZ of day 35 WT human forebrain organoids (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a methodological description of the experimental procedure.

claim: Constructs were generated that expressed CRE-ERT2 and shRNA on a retroviral backbone.
source: To ensure constitutive expression of shRNA and recombination of only the cells expressing the shRNA, we generated constructs that expressed CRE-ERT2 and the shRNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) on a retroviral backbone.
evidence: This is a methodological description of construct generation.

claim: Day 24 organoids derived from Centriolin-RITE hESCs were transduced with either scrambled or Ninein-targeting shRNA retroviruses.
source: Day 24 organoids derived from Centriolin-RITE (CRE-ERT2 negative) hESCs were transduced with either scrambled or Ninein-targeting shRNA retroviruses (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a methodological description of the experimental procedure.

claim: Organoids were induced with 4-OH tamoxifen and fixed 22 days later for centrosome color analysis.
source: Organoids were induced with 4-OH tamoxifen, fixed 22 days later and their centrosomes colours were manually analysed (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a methodological description of the experimental procedure.

claim: The Centriolin-RITE tool presents benefits over photoconversion-based approaches.
source: Nevertheless, the Centriolin-RITE tool kit presents a number of potential benefits over the previously described photoconversion-based approach (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a comparative assessment of methodological approaches.

claim: The addition of high-affinity biochemical tags to the RITE cassette is feasible and will allow for further biochemical and proteomics-based analyses.
source: This facilitates biochemical separation of the birthdated proteins by immunoprecipitation; further, the addition of high-affinity biochemical tags to the RITE cassette is feasible and will allow for further biochemical and proteomics-based analyses, which are essential to untangling the complex protein–protein interactions in centrosomes (O'Neill et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications of the tool.

claim: Using Centriolin-RITE in human brain organoids will allow future experiments studying whether centrosomal age differs between apical and basal radial glia cells.
source: Furthermore, using it in human brain organoids will allow future experiments studying whether centrosomal age differs between apical and basal radial glia cells, the latter one being rare in brains of lisencephalic animals (Camp et al., 2015; Pollen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications, supported by citations about basal radial glia.

claim: Basal radial glia cells are rare in brains of lisencephalic animals.
source: Furthermore, using it in human brain organoids will allow future experiments studying whether centrosomal age differs between apical and basal radial glia cells, the latter one being rare in brains of lisencephalic animals (Camp et al., 2015; Pollen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Camp et al., 2015 and Pollen et al., 2015.

claim: The signal of Centriolin-RITE is too dim to perform live imaging or clonal analyses with current technical approaches.
source: This reduces potential artefacts of excess protein expression; however, endogenous tagging provides only few fluorophores per centrosome to be visualised. Therefore, the signal is too dim to, with current technical approaches, perform live imaging or clonal analyses to follow individual centrosomes and their subsequent segregation.
evidence: This is a limitation of the method based on experimental observations.

claim: Endogenous tagging of centriolin reduces potential artefacts of excess protein expression compared to overexpression approaches.
source: In the study presented here, centriolin was endogenously tagged with fluorophores, in contrast to previous approaches relying on overexpression of centrosomal proteins. This reduces potential artefacts of excess protein expression; however, endogenous tagging provides only few fluorophores per centrosome to be visualised.
evidence: This is a methodological advantage inferred from the experimental design.

claim: NPCs in VZ were selected for comparison because their presence in the VZ strongly indicates their capacity for self-renewal.
source: NPCs in VZ were selected for comparison, as opposed to all SOX2-positive cells, as their presence in the VZ strongly indicates their capacity for self-renewal whereas SOX2-positive cells outside of the VZ may have already started differentiation along the neural lineage.
evidence: This is a methodological justification based on knowledge of NPC biology.

claim: SOX2-positive cells outside of the VZ may have already started differentiation along the neural lineage.
source: NPCs in VZ were selected for comparison, as opposed to all SOX2-positive cells, as their presence in the VZ strongly indicates their capacity for self-renewal whereas SOX2-positive cells outside of the VZ may have already started differentiation along the neural lineage.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of neural differentiation and SOX2 expression patterns.

claim: The 3D tissue imaging process collapses the tissue into a 2D image, which can lead to inclusion of centrosomes whose cell bodies are not imaged.
source: During this process, the 3D tissue gets collapsed into a 2D image. As ventricle-like structures in organoids are tubular or spherical in nature, this dimension collapse produces a circle of centrosomes, where multiple Z planes show a ring (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B). This leads to an inclusion of centrosomes whose-cell bodies are not imaged because of the radial orientation of NPCs relative to the ventricles and the volume of tissue imaged.
evidence: This is a methodological consideration based on imaging geometry.

claim: Images were digitally subdivided into areas of recombined NPCs and their likely progeny to correct for potential data skewing.
source: To correct for this, images were digitally subdivided into areas of recombined NPCs and their likely progeny (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a methodological approach to address a potential confound.

claim: Orange centrosomes' tdTomato signals were visibly indistinguishable from non-recombined centrosomes.
source: Orange centrosomes' tdTomato signals were visibly indistinguishable from non-recombined centrosomes (Figure 2F); yellow centrosomes had some tdTomato signal but less compared to non-recombined centrosomes and green centrosomes showed no detectable tdTomato signal.
evidence: This is a description of the manual color allocation criteria used in the analysis.

claim: Yellow centrosomes had some tdTomato signal but less compared to non-recombined centrosomes.
source: Orange centrosomes' tdTomato signals were visibly indistinguishable from non-recombined centrosomes (Figure 2F); yellow centrosomes had some tdTomato signal but less compared to non-recombined centrosomes and green centrosomes showed no detectable tdTomato signal.
evidence: This is a description of the manual color allocation criteria used in the analysis.

claim: Green centrosomes showed no detectable tdTomato signal.
source: Orange centrosomes' tdTomato signals were visibly indistinguishable from non-recombined centrosomes (Figure 2F); yellow centrosomes had some tdTomato signal but less compared to non-recombined centrosomes and green centrosomes showed no detectable tdTomato signal.
evidence: This is a description of the manual color allocation criteria used in the analysis.

claim: There was no difference in the localisation of yellow centrosomes between ventricular and non-ventricular regions.
source: The inverse was observed for green centrosomes, whereas there was no difference seen in the localisation of yellow centrosomes, similar to what was observed in the absolute number of each centrosome colour (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a finding from the centrosome color analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: An unbiased method of analysing fluorescence levels at centrosomes was used to validate the manual approach.
source: To validate the manual approach, we used an unbiased method of analysing fluorescence levels at the centrosomes. The mean tdTomato and NeonGreen signal was acquired, and a ratio was calculated for each centrosome (see Methods for details).
evidence: This is a methodological description of the validation approach.

claim: Centrosomes were divided into thirds by their NeonGreen to total signal ratio for automated color allocation.
source: Next, centrosomes were divided into thirds by their NeonGreen to total signal ratio, with the highest, middle, and lowest thirds being labelled 'green', 'yellow', and 'orange', respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological description of the automated analysis approach.

claim: Automated color calling showed increased orange centrosomes in the VZ and more green centrosomes in the non-ventricle areas.
source: Again, we found increased orange centrosomes in the VZ and more green centrosomes in the non-ventricle areas within organoids (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E, Figure 2—source data 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the automated analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-E.
